source.title: Answer to Some Open Problems and Global Bifurcation for an Overdetermined Problem

accepted.question_text: Let s → (w_s, T_s) be the local smooth bifurcation family from Theorem 1.1, where for each small s the modified cylinder Ω_s = {(x, t) ∈ R^n × R : |x| < 1 + s cos(2π t / T_s) + s w_s(2π t / T_s)} carries a positive T_s-periodic solution of the overdetermined eigenvalue problem Δu + λu = 0 in Ω_s, u = 0 on ∂Ω_s, and ⟨∇u, ν⟩ = const on ∂Ω_s. When Ω_s is viewed as a domain in R^n × R/T_sZ, is Ω_s a local minimizer of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue functional Ω → λ_1(Ω)?
accepted.context_brief: Local minimality of bifurcating extremal domains

evidence.quote: for each s ∈ (−ε, ε), (1.2) has a positive Ts-periodic solution us ∈ C2,α(Ωs ) on the modified cylinder Ωs = {(x, t) ∈ Rn × R : |x| < 1 + s cos(2π t/Ts) + sws(2π t/Ts)}.
Open Problem 1. Are the extremal domains Ωs in Rn ×R/TsZ (local) minima for the functional Ω → λ1(Ω)?
Note that Ωs may or may not be local minima for the functional Ω → λ1(Ω). Although we offer clarification for solving Open Problem 1, it remains open.

accepted.question_text: For the same local bifurcation family s → (w_s, T_s) from Theorem 1.1, determine the type of bifurcation at the critical period T*(n): is it subcritical, critical, or supercritical? Equivalently, determine whether ∂_s T(s)|_{s=0} is negative, zero, or positive.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. Is the bifurcation at T∗(n) sub-critical, critical, or super-critical? In other words, ∂s (Ts )|s=0 < 0, ∂s (Ts )|s=0 = 0, or ∂s (Ts )|s=0 > 0?

Theorem 1.2. Under the assumptions of Theorem 1.1, ∂s (T (s))|s=0 = 0. It is known from Theorem 1.2 that the bifurcation at T∗(n) is critical. Consequently, the conclusion of Theorem 1.2 gives an affirmative answer to the above Open Problem 2.

accepted.question_text: Starting from the local branch in Theorem 1.1 at the bifurcation point (0, T*(n)) in C^{2,α}_{even,0}(R/2πZ) × R, can that branch be extended globally? More concretely, do there exist nontrivial branches C^+ and C^- emanating from (0, T*(n)) such that every (v^ν, T) on a branch yields a positive T-periodic solution of Δu + λu = 0 on the modified cylinder Ω^ν = {(x, t) ∈ R^n × R : |x| < 1 + v^ν(2π t/T)}, with each branch either unbounded or meeting the boundary of O = {v > -1} × (0, +∞)?
accepted.context_brief: Global continuation of the local branch

evidence.quote: Finally, a natural question is whether the branch in Theorem 1.1 can be extended to the global? Another aim of this paper is to study the global structure of the branch obtained in Theorem 1.1.
Theorem 1.4. There are two nontrivial branches C+, C− in C2,αeven,0(R/2πZ)×R emanating from (0, T∗(n)) ... Moreover, either Cν is unbounded or Cν ∩ ∂O ≠ ∅.
